captions.title: 1. Daily campus energy trend
captions.observation: Campus load shows weekday peaks and exam-period lift in library/lab demand.

captions.title: 2. Building-wise consumption
captions.observation: Hostels and computer labs dominate total energy due to occupancy duration and IT/HVAC load.

captions.title: 3. Building × hour energy heatmap
captions.observation: Academic blocks peak 09:00–16:00; hostels invert with night-time occupancy.

captions.title: 4. Peak hour analysis
captions.observation: Mean interval energy rises through late morning and remains elevated until evening hostel load.

captions.title: 5. Weather vs energy
captions.observation: Higher outdoor temperature correlates with AC-driven energy, especially above ~29°C.

captions.title: 6. Occupancy vs energy
captions.observation: Energy scales with occupancy but HVAC/IT rooms sit above the occupancy-only trend.

captions.title: 7. Device contribution proxy
captions.observation: Air-conditioning is the largest controllable contributor whenever outdoor temperature is high.

captions.title: 8. Weekly / monthly-scale trend
captions.observation: Weekly totals are stable with a late-July exam-window increase.

captions.title: 9. Weekend vs weekday
captions.observation: Weekday academic/admin load exceeds weekends; hostels remain relatively sticky.

captions.title: 10. Top-20 room utilization
captions.observation: Library halls and cafeteria dining rooms show the highest average occupancy ratios.

captions.title: 11. Category mean energy intensity
captions.observation: Computer labs have the highest mean intensity due to dense IT load plus HVAC.

captions.title: 12. Working-hours energy split
captions.observation: Working hours raise academic energy; after-hours residual load is a wastage target.

captions.title: 13. Humidity vs energy
captions.observation: Humidity is weakly associated with energy; temperature and occupancy dominate.

captions.title: 14. Active devices vs energy
captions.observation: Mean energy increases monotonically with concurrently active end-use devices.

captions.title: 15. Cooling load index vs energy
captions.observation: Cooling load index is a strong engineered predictor of HVAC-dominated intervals.

captions.title: 16. Power factor distribution
captions.observation: Power factor clusters near 0.90–0.96; AC-on intervals pull PF slightly lower.

captions.title: 17. Voltage distribution
captions.observation: Branch voltage stays around the 230 V Indian nominal with realistic feeder noise.

captions.title: 18. Indoor vs outdoor temperature
captions.observation: Indoor temperatures are suppressed relative to outdoor when HVAC is active.

captions.title: 19. Day-of-week energy
captions.observation: Monday–Friday academic schedules produce higher campus totals than weekends.

captions.title: 20. Occupancy heatmap by category
captions.observation: Hostels fill overnight; cafeteria peaks at lunch; library occupancy rises in the exam window.

captions.title: 21. Mean building utilization
captions.observation: Admin utilization is high during workdays but low absolute energy due to smaller rooms.

captions.title: 22. AC operating profile
captions.observation: AC duty cycle tracks hot working hours — the primary HVAC optimization lever.

captions.title: 23. Empty-room lighting wastage share
captions.observation: About 0.12% of intervals show lights on with zero occupancy — a lighting-control target.

captions.title: 24. Building weekend vs weekday intensity
captions.observation: Academic buildings drop sharply on weekends; hostels do not, confirming schedule-aware controls.
